correctness.rationale: For L_r=h_3(F_q)⊕F_q^r with Z=span(z,c_1,…,c_r) and 2-dimensional symplectic quotient V, every Lie subalgebra A is classified by P=π(A)≤V, C=A∩Z, and a graph map P→Z/C; for dim(P)=2 closure forces z∈C, while dim(P)≤1 is automatic. Counting the three strata gives N_r=G_(r+1)+(q+1)A_(r+1)+B_r. Nonpermuting ordered pairs require two different one-dimensional quotient lines and z∉C+D. Writing C,D as graphs over subspaces U,T≤F_q^r, the functional compatibility on U∩T leaves q^{2r+2−dim(U∩T)} choices for a fixed ordered pair of distinct quotient lines, giving bad=q^{2r+3}(q+1)J_r with J_r=Σ_{U,T}q^{−dim(U∩T)}; the Gaussian-binomial h,a,b formula counts all such pairs without overcount. Dominant Gaussian degrees give, for even r, one leading N and J term so bad/N²→1; for odd r, N leading coefficient 2 and J coefficient 3 so bad/N²→3/4, giving sd→0 and 1/4 respectively. Independent Gaussian finite sums for q=2,3,5,7,11 and r=0..4 matched specializations and bounded probabilities; separate direct complete subspace/bracket enumeration over F2 yielded (r,N,bad)=(0,12,24),(1,43,336),(2,198,7584), matching formulas. Large-q numerical limits are corroboration; the parity law follows from polynomial leading-degree analysis.
